Abstract
Recent advancements in diffusion models have significantly improved text-to-image generation, enabling their application to visual storytelling, where coherent image sequences are generated from narrative prompts. However, existing methods primarily focus on identity preservation and often fail to adapt to diverse scene variations, resulting in semantic misalignment and structural inflexibility. We propose EOS-Story, a training-free framework that harmonizes identity consistency with scene-specific adaptation across text and vision spaces.
In the text space, we decouple the narrative into identity and scene sub-prompts to prevent information dilution, but this leaves the scene without access to appearance cues.
To bridge this gap, we introduce Cross-Contextual Bridging, which softly injects a phrase-level appearance residual into the scene’s
⟨
\langle
EOS
⟩
\rangle
embedding. In the vision space, we find that scale mismatch between identity and scene subjects causes a few identity tokens to be repeatedly transferred, producing structural artifacts. We address this with Adaptive Identity Preservation, which anchors identity features at the scene-specific scale (Identity Anchoring) and integrates them via Identity-Aware Self-Attention. To evaluate performance under varied spatial compositions, we extend the Consistory+ benchmark with diverse framing scenarios (Consistory+_+). Extensive experiments show that EOS-Story achieves competitive or superior performance on both benchmarks.

5
Conclusion
In this work, we propose
EOS-Story
, a training-free framework that adaptively models scene-specific variance in visual storytelling across text and vision spaces. We introduce
Cross-Contextual Bridging
, which decouples the narrative into identity and scene sub-prompts and bridges the resulting semantic gap by injecting phrase-level appearance residuals into the scene’s
⟨
\langle
EOS
⟩
\rangle
embedding. To complement this with structural adaptation, we further propose
Adaptive Identity Preservation
, which anchors subject features at the scene-specific scale and refines integration through Identity-Aware Self-Attention. To evaluate scene adaptability, we extend Consistory+ with diverse framing variations (Consistory+_+).
Extensive experiments show that EOS-Story achieves competitive or superior performance in both prompt fidelity and structural adaptability.

Appendix 0.B
Consistory+_+ & Framing Evaluation Details
The ShotBench
[
15
]
includes a wide range of framing phrases across eight categories (
Tab.
7
).
To ensure a focused and rigorous evaluation of scene-specific structural variance, we intentionally restricted the scope to three primary categories, excluding the remaining five based on the following methodological criteria: (1) Prompt Redundancy: Shot Framing descriptors (e.g., “single”, “2 shot”) primarily specify the number of characters, which is already inherently defined by the subject phrases in the storyboard prompts; (2) Redundancy Mitigation: Lens Size phrases (e.g., “wide lens”) are largely redundant as they are semantically encompassed by the Shot Size category (“wide shot”); (3) Domain Incompatibility: Camera Movement is inherently applicable to temporal video sequences and is thus irrelevant to static image generation; and (4) Task Relevance: Lighting-related categories fall outside the scope of our work, as they primarily focus on stylistic or artistic variations rather than the structural and compositional elements that define scene-specific variance.
Framing Phrase Filtering.
Although SDXL generally produces textually well-aligned images, it sometimes struggles to accurately reflect specific framing phrases.
Before incorporating these phrases into our benchmark extension, we first evaluate how well they are captured by the base SDXL model using the ShotBench evaluation mechanism.
To quantitatively assess phrase reflection, we construct approximately 90 diverse scene prompts and append each framing phrase at the end (e.g., “A photo of a woman baking cookies, close-up shot”).
We generate images for 10 random seeds per phrase and compute the top-1 and top-3 accuracy, along with standard deviations, as shown in
Fig.
16
.
For example, in the “shot size” category with 7 phrase options, this results in a total of 6,300 images (90 scenes × 7 phrases × 10 seeds).
We filter out framing phrases whose top-1 accuracy is zero (e.g., “extreme wide shot”), as these are not reliably reflected in the generated outputs from SDXL.
Consistory+_+
With the remaining framing phrases, we extend the original Consistory+ benchmark using GPT-4o.
Since these phrases are visually meaningful primarily for animate subjects, we first guide GPT-4o to determine whether the subject in each prompt is animate.
Then, the model is instructed to append the most appropriate framing phrase for the given scene, resulting in Consistory+_+.
Framing Accuracy Evaluation.
Following the evaluation protocol in
[
15
]
, we provide the generated image along with the corresponding framing category (e.g., shot size) and prompt the model with a multiple-choice question.
For instance, for shot size evaluation, we prompt the model with a multiple-choice question such as
“What is the shot size of this shot?” and provide predefined options (e.g., wide shot, medium shot, close-up shot).
The predicted category is compared against the framing phrase specified in the text prompt, and accuracy is reported.

Layer Application Variation.
We apply Identity Anchoring (IA) and Identity-Aware Self-Attention (IASA) at different layers of the unet decoder in the diffusion model.
While prior works typically transfer identity-related features within the decoder (up-block) layers, we further investigate the impact of layer selection.

Interestingly, when IA and IASA are applied to configurations that include the up-block layers, the CLIP-I score notably improves (surpassing 0.880).
These results empirically highlight the importance of the decoder layers (up-blocks) in effectively conveying identity features and enhancing the image quality during generation.

article.headline: 免训练框架让角色随场景自适应
article.lede: 免训练框架 EOS-Story 把叙事拆成身份与场景子提示，用 ⟨EOS⟩ 残差补回外观线索，Consistory+ 上
article.problem: 现有视觉叙事方法大多只盯着身份保持，把整段叙事当成单一提示编码，长提示中的外观与场景细节容易被稀释，导致语义错位；在视觉侧又是空间盲的特征注入，不理会每个场景的机位与主体尺度。结果是同一角色在不同场景里姿态僵硬、结构重复，与场景提示对齐变弱。
article.method: 作者提出免训练框架 EOS-Story，分文本与视觉两路处理场景差异。文本侧 Cross-Contextual Bridging 把输入拆成 style、subject、appearance、scene 四部分，用身份提示与风格-主体锚点之间的 ⟨EOS⟩ 嵌入差作为外观残差，加到场景提示的 ⟨EOS⟩ 上，在不加长场景描述的前提下补回外观。视觉侧 Adaptive Identity Preservation 先用 Identity Anchoring 把身份特征缩放到与场景主体一致的尺寸并做置信度（μ+σ）过滤的匹配融合，再用 Identity-Aware Self-Attention 让场景特征选择性关注身份特征。
article.results: 在 Consistory+ 上，EOS-Story 的 CLIP-T 为 0.9042（SDXL 基线 0.8971），DreamSim 0.2005（基线 0.3124，越低越好），Aesthetic 6.1764、ImageReward 1.1680，均高于 Consistory 的 6.1070 与 0.9814；但 CLIP-I 为 0.8850，低于 IP-Adapter 的 0.9398。在作者扩展的 Consistory+_+ 上，CLIP-T 0.8998、DreamSim 0.2146、ImageReward 1.3217。20 人、40 个故事板的用户研究中，EOS-Story 在 52.8% 的样本里被评为最佳；生成 5 个故事占用 47777 MB 显存、耗时 118.570 秒。
article.why_it_matters: 它把 CLIP 的 ⟨EOS⟩ 当作可加残差的语义控制点，给出一条不改模型权重、也无需重训的场景自适应路线，并可迁移到 SD3（CLIP-T 0.8978）；这提示叙事生成的关键不只是身份保持，还有文本与视觉两个空间里的场景适配。
article.limitations: 方法依赖跨注意力图当主体掩码，偶尔会圈错区域造成错位，论文也承认这是与前作共有的问题，且 SDXL 主干本身对某些概念（如 faun）直接生成失败。Cross-Contextual Bridging 依赖 CLIP 的 ⟨EOS⟩ 语义，无法直接用于 T5 或 LLM 文本编码器，FLUX 上只能单独使用 AIP；此外 CLIP-I 并未超过 IP-Adapter，评测也主要围绕 Consistory 系列基准。
article.figure_caption_zh: EOS-Story 流程示意：文本空间把外观残差注入场景的 ⟨EOS⟩ 嵌入，视觉空间先按场景主体尺度锚定身份特征，再经身份感知自注意力融合。

page_papers.title: Drift, Then Spread: Learning One-Step Generative Policies for Online Reinforcement Learning
page_papers.abstract: Generative policies offer expressive action distributions for online reinforcement learning (RL), but many diffusion- and flow-based policies require costly iterative sampling. We propose DriftSpread, a one-step generative policy based on Drifting for online maximum-entropy (MaxEnt) RL. To incorporate entropy without a tractable policy density, we build on an energy-based view of Drifting and derive critic-guided Drift and entropy-induced Spread from the negative MaxEnt objective. Our method learns these updates sequentially in the same actor, using action regression for value improvement and distribution matching to capture the effect of entropy. The actor updates require neither direct samples from the critic-defined Boltzmann target nor policy-density or score estimation. Under exact fitting with a fixed critic, we prove convergence to the Boltzmann target in the small-step limit followed by the long-time limit. On MuJoCo, DriftSpread achieves the highest aggregate normalized return among all evaluated methods, while outperforming the diffusion- and flow-based baselines in both training and inference efficiency.
page_papers.content:
Drift, Then Spread: Learning One-Step Generative Policies for Online Reinforcement Learning
Chunyu Luo
Hongyu Zhao
Guangyi Ni
Yue Song
Lingkai Kong
The University of Hong Kong  Beihang University
Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen  Independent Researcher  Tsinghua University
Correspondence to:
lingkaikong@hku.hk
.
Abstract
Generative policies offer expressive action distributions
for online reinforcement learning (RL), but many diffusion-
and flow-based policies require costly iterative sampling.
We propose
DriftSpread
, a one-step generative policy based on
Drifting for online maximum-entropy (MaxEnt) RL.
To incorporate entropy without a tractable policy density,
we build on an energy-based view of Drifting and derive
critic-guided Drift and entropy-induced Spread from the
negative MaxEnt objective.
Our method learns these updates sequentially in the same
actor, using action regression for value improvement and
distribution matching to capture the effect of entropy.
The actor updates require neither direct samples from
the critic-defined Boltzmann target nor policy-density
or score estimation.
Under exact fitting with a fixed critic, we prove
convergence to the Boltzmann target in the small-step
limit followed by the long-time limit.
On MuJoCo,
DriftSpread
achieves the highest aggregate
normalized return among all evaluated methods,
while outperforming the diffusion- and flow-based
baselines in both training and inference efficiency.

Generative policies offer expressive action distributions
for online reinforcement learning (RL).
Diffusion- and flow-based policies can capture multimodal
distributions that are difficult to represent with a single
Gaussian
(
Dong et al., 2025
;
Celik et al., 2025
)
.
However, many of these approaches generate actions through
iterative sampling, requiring repeated network evaluations
during training and inference.
Recent MeanFlow-based methods reduce this cost through
few-step or one-step action generation
(
Dong et al., 2026
;
Chen et al., 2025
;
Kim et al., 2026
)
.
Drifting offers a different way to train one-step
generators
(
Deng et al., 2026
)
.
At each training iteration, it uses target data to
move generated samples toward the desired distribution,
then trains the generator to reproduce the moved
samples from the same inputs.
Through these repeated updates, the generator learns
to produce samples from the target distribution in
a single forward pass at inference.
This approach has shown better performance than
MeanFlow variants in one-step image generation on
ImageNet
(
Deng et al., 2026
)
.
These results motivate exploring Drifting for online
RL, where its use remains less studied.
We consider the maximum-entropy (MaxEnt) RL objective,
which balances expected return with policy entropy
to encourage exploration
(
Haarnoja et al., 2018
)
.
The critic defines a Boltzmann target distribution
for policy improvement, but does not directly provide
samples from it
(
Li et al., 2026
)
.
We therefore adopt an energy-based view of Drifting
(
Gretton et al., 2026
;
Han et al., 2026
)
,
using the negative MaxEnt policy-improvement objective
as the energy.
This energy guides updates to actions generated by
the current policy.
For the value term, critic gradients tell us how to
move actions toward higher values.
The entropy term is harder to use: an implicit actor
generates actions but does not provide a tractable
density for computing their distribution’s entropy.
We therefore need training targets that capture
the effect of entropy without explicitly computing it.
We propose
DriftSpread
, a one-step generative policy in the
Drifting model family for online MaxEnt RL.
Our key idea is to derive two updates from this energy
and fit them sequentially to the same actor through
repeated Drift–Spread cycles.
In each cycle, Drift uses critic gradients to move
generated actions toward higher values.
The actor then learns to reproduce these updated
actions from the same inputs through regression.
Spread captures the entropy contribution through
diffusion of the action distribution.
We approximate this diffusion by adding appropriately
scaled independent noise to actions from the updated
actor, then train the actor to match the resulting
distribution.
This allows the actor to learn the effect of entropy
without explicitly computing it.
For a fixed critic, we prove
that the learned policy converges to the Boltzmann
target distribution in the small-step, long-time limit.
Our main contributions are:
(1) We introduce
DriftSpread
, a Drifting model for online
MaxEnt RL with expressive policies and one-step action
generation.
(2) We develop sequential Drift–Spread training through
critic-guided regression and entropy regularization to
address the challenge of entropy computation for implicit
policies.
(3) On MuJoCo,
DriftSpread
outperforms 13 baselines
in aggregate normalized return, with lower training
costs than the diffusion, flow, and MeanFlow baselines
(Figure
1
).
2
Related Work
Generative policies for online RL.
Diffusion and flow models provide expressive action
distributions for online RL.
One line of work optimizes policies by backpropagating
critic gradients through diffusion or flow sampling
(
Wang et al., 2024
;
Lyu et al., 2025
)
.
DIME also differentiates through diffusion sampling
while optimizing a variational lower bound on the
MaxEnt objective
(
Celik et al., 2025
)
.
Another line of work constructs training targets
for learning critic-defined Boltzmann distributions.
DQS uses weighted averages of critic gradients
to construct score targets
(
Jain et al., 2025
)
.
SDAC and MaxEntDP instead use critic values to weight
denoising supervision and noise estimates, respectively
(
Ma et al., 2025
;
Dong et al., 2025
)
.
Reverse flow matching unifies these gradient-expectation
and noise-expectation formulations through posterior-mean
estimation
(
Li et al., 2026
)
.
These approaches use iterative action sampling,
motivating few-step and one-step policies for online RL.
MeanFlow was introduced for one-step generative modeling
and learns average velocities
(
Geng et al., 2025
)
.
Recent online RL methods use this formulation
to learn policies with fewer generation steps.
FPMD trains rectified-flow and MeanFlow policies
through policy mirror descent, with both variants
supporting one-step inference
(
Chen et al., 2025
)
.
MFPO trains few-step MeanFlow policies using velocity
estimates for critic-defined Boltzmann targets
(
Dong et al., 2026
)
, while SOM constructs velocity
targets from critic-based score estimates to train
one-step MeanFlow policies
(
Kim et al., 2026
)
.
Drifting models and policy learning.
Drifting learns one-step generators by repeatedly
moving generated samples and training the generator
to reproduce their updated positions.
This approach has achieved state-of-the-art performance
in one-step image generation on ImageNet
(
Deng et al., 2026
)
.
Subsequent work relates specific Drifting fields
to Wasserstein gradient flows
(
Gretton et al., 2026
)
and uses
optimal-transport couplings to construct sample
updates
(
He et al., 2026
)
.
W-Flow derives sample movements from an objective
over distributions and trains a one-step generator
on the resulting samples
(
Han et al., 2026
)
.
Drifting has also been applied to policy learning.
For offline RL, DriftQL combines critic-guided
policy improvement with a Drifting regularizer
based on the behavior distribution
(
Houssaini et al., 2026
)
.
For offline-to-online RL, Drifting Field Policy
derives a KL-regularized policy update through
Wasserstein gradient flow and constructs training
targets from actions ranked by the critic
(
Koo et al., 2026
)
.
Our work focuses on online MaxEnt RL from scratch.

Conclusion and Limitations
We introduced
DriftSpread
, a Drifting-based approach to
learning expressive one-step policies for online RL.
Building on an energy-based view of Drifting, we derive
critic-guided Drift and entropy-induced Spread from
the MaxEnt objective.
The two updates are learned sequentially by the same
actor: Drift moves actions toward higher values,
while Spread matches a broader distribution constructed
from the updated actor.
This design incorporates the effect of entropy without
estimating policy densities or scores, while allowing
each action sample to be generated in one forward pass.
Under exact fitting, our analysis establishes convergence
to the fixed-critic Boltzmann target in the small-step,
long-time limit.
MuJoCo experiments show that
DriftSpread
combines strong
control performance with efficient training and inference,
supporting Drifting as a practical approach to
generative policy learning.
Our work leaves two directions for future research.
First, our evaluation is limited to simulation
environments.
Testing on real-world control tasks would help
assess robustness to observation noise and changes
in system dynamics.
Second, we use a fixed spreading-noise distribution
and scale during training.
Adapting the spreading strength as learning progresses
may better balance exploration and value improvement.

article.headline: 先漂移后扩散：在线RL的一步生成策略
article.lede: 用critic梯度漂移、熵诱导扩散，一步生成动作；MuJoCo聚合回报最高，推理0.15毫秒。
article.problem: 扩散与流策略能表达多模态动作分布，但采样需要反复评估网络，训练和推理代价高。最大熵RL还要求策略熵，而隐式actor不给出可解析密度，无法直接计算score或熵。critic只定义了Boltzmann目标分布，却不提供该分布的样本。
article.method: 作者把负最大熵目标当作能量，由Wasserstein梯度流得到速度场∇Q−λ∇logπ，并转写为连续性方程：critic引导的漂移项加上λΔπ的扩散项。实现上，Drift把动作沿critic梯度移动后用回归拟合，Spread则对更新后actor的动作加零均值、协方差2ληI的噪声，用MMD（经特征函数计算）做分布匹配。两步顺序更新同一个actor，既不需要策略密度也不需要score估计，推理时一次前向即可出动作。
article.results: 在HalfCheetah、Hopper、Walker2d、Ant、Humanoid五个MuJoCo-v3任务上，每个方法训练10^6次环境交互、5个随机种子，DriftSpread在13个基线中取得最高的聚合归一化回报。平均推理时间0.15毫秒/动作，而DIME为1.24毫秒、两步MeanFlow策略MFPO为0.36毫秒；训练成本低于扩散、流和MeanFlow基线，但DFP与WPPG的训练时间略低。HalfCheetah-v3和Walker2d-v3上后期平均回报最高。附录的高斯玩具例中，顺序拟合最终KL为0.000422，联合拟合为0.512165。
article.why_it_matters: 它把生成策略的迭代采样成本压到一次前向，同时保留多模态表达能力，并给出固定critic下收敛到Boltzmann目标的证明，为一步生成策略进入在线RL提供了可分析的路径。
article.limitations: 收敛保证只在固定critic、每次更新精确拟合、步长趋于零且时间趋于无穷的极限下成立，并不覆盖实际在线训练中critic与actor同时变化的情形。实验仅限MuJoCo仿真，未验证真实系统；扩散噪声的分布与尺度全程固定，且相比DFP、WPPG训练时间略长。
article.figure_caption_zh: 图2：DriftSpread总览——(a) critic学习与顺序的Drift–Spread actor更新交替进行，同一actor在不同阶段都从参考噪声一步生成动作；(b) 负最大熵目标示意，Drift把动作推向高价值区，Spread再拓宽漂移后的分布以体现熵的作用。

The maps $f_ $ represent the same actor at different training stages, each generating an action sample from reference noise in one forward pass. (b) The surface schematically represents the negative MaxEnt objective over policy distributions. The samples below illustrate how Drift moves actions toward higher critic values and Spread then broadens the post-Drift distribution to capture the effect of entropy.

page_papers.title: Easy-3Dfy: Object-Level Geometric Composition for Single-Image 3D Scene Construction
page_papers.abstract: Single-image 3D scene construction is a fundamental problem in 3D vision. Recent methods such as SAM-3Dfy enable end-to-end reconstruction of 3D assets and their scene layouts, but still struggle with fine-grained scene geometry and asset quality. Meanwhile, specialized 3D object generators provide detailed object geometry, while 3D foundation models offer strong and generalizable spatial understanding. We propose Easy-3Dfy, a compositional workflow that decouples object generation from scene layout estimation, allowing specialized models to fully exploit their respective strengths. An RPF-based aligner then bridges these capabilities by establishing geometric correspondence between object-local meshes and partial scene pointmaps, recovering object layout for scene composition. Without requiring complete scene-level supervision, the proposed workflow consistently outperforms SAM-3Dfy across multiple geometric metrics on Scene-Maker and 3D-FUTURE200. Our results demonstrate that explicit geometric composition can effectively combine high-quality object generation with strong spatial understanding, while enabling the workflow to benefit independently from advances in both 3D object generation and foundation models.

Easy-3Dfy: Object-Level Geometric Composition for Single-Image 3D Scene Construction

Abstract
Single-image 3D scene construction is a fundamental problem in 3D vision. Recent methods such as SAM-3Dfy enable end-to-end reconstruction of 3D assets and their scene layouts, but still struggle with fine-grained scene geometry and asset quality. Meanwhile, specialized 3D object generators provide detailed object geometry, while 3D foundation models offer strong and generalizable spatial understanding. We propose
Easy-3Dfy
, a compositional workflow that decouples object generation from scene layout estimation, allowing specialized models to fully exploit their respective strengths. An RPF-based aligner then bridges these capabilities by establishing geometric correspondence between object-local meshes and partial scene pointmaps, recovering object layout for scene composition. Without requiring complete scene-level supervision, the proposed workflow consistently outperforms SAM-3Dfy across multiple geometric metrics on Scene-Maker and 3D-FUTURE200. Our results demonstrate that explicit geometric composition can effectively combine high-quality object generation with strong spatial understanding, while enabling the workflow to benefit independently from advances in both 3D object generation and foundation models.

Qualitative comparison on multi-object scenes.
Given a single image and its object masks, Easy-3Dfy improves object layout and produces more coherent scene assemblies across general examples.
1
Introduction
Single-image 3D scene construction is a fundamental problem in 3D vision, aiming to recover a set of complete 3D object assets and arrange them in a common metric coordinate system from a single image. Recent advances have made substantial progress toward this goal. In particular, SAM-3Dfy
(
SAM 3D Team et al., 2025
)
provides an end-to-end framework that jointly addresses openset object asset generation and scene layout estimation, demonstrating the feasibility of reconstructing complete 3D scenes from a single image. However, jointly addressing these capabilities within a scene-level pipeline can limit the fine-grained quality of both generated assets and spatial layouts. The object assets produced by such scene-oriented systems can remain less detailed than those from specialized 3D object generation models, while the lack of explicit geometric alignment can lead to interpenetrating and floating object layouts.
Figure 2:
Overview of Easy-3Dfy.
Given object masks, a spatial model predicts a scene pointmap. For each object, an image editor produces a completed object image and a replaceable image-to-3D provider generates a local mesh. The RPF-based aligner matches its anchor point cloud to the object-specific partial query extracted from the pointmap, predicts correspondence positions, and recovers a uniform-scale similarity transform via Umeyama fitting. Transforming all complete meshes assembles the final scene.
Meanwhile, recent progress in 3D foundation models has provided strong alternatives for the two complementary capabilities involved in scene construction. In particular, 3D object generation models can produce increasingly complete and detailed object assets, while monocular pointmap reconstruction models provide strong scene-level spatial cues. Such decoupling allows each type of model to fully exploit its specialized capability, while making the overall scene construction workflow naturally extensible to future advances in either direction.
Building on these complementary capabilities, we introduce
Easy-3Dfy
, a compositional workflow that reformulates single-image 3D scene construction as an object-level point cloud registration problem. Specifically, given a complete object asset and the corresponding partial scene point cloud, the goal is to estimate the transformation from the asset-local coordinate system to the scene coordinate system. To address this, Easy-3Dfy incorporates a Rectified Point Flow Model (RPF) aligner to resolve geometric correspondence and recover the relative transform parameters between the two point sets. Specifically, RPF operates as a generative registration model that directly synthesizes surface-aligned point clouds conditioned on the object asset and the scene point cloud, establishing robust point-to-point relationships. This aligner acts as a critical geometric bridge, allowing the independent object generation and scene reconstruction modules to function collaboratively within a unified framework.
To compare and validate the scene geometric construction capability of Easy-3Dfy, we first evaluate the quality of asset composition and scene layout produced by Easy-3Dfy and SAM-3Dfy using the same generated object assets on Scene-Maker
(
Shi et al., 2025
)
and 3D-FUTURE200
(
Fu et al., 2021
)
. Easy-3Dfy consistently improves multiple geometric metrics at the scene-level, demonstrating that explicit geometric alignment is effective for high-quality scene construction. Furthermore, by replacing the underlying 3D object generation models, we observe that Easy-3Dfy can further benefit from improvements in upstream object generation, indicating the scalability of the proposed decoupled workflow.
Our contributions are summarized as follows:
•
We propose
Easy-3Dfy
, a compositional workflow for single-image 3D scene construction that decouples object asset generation from scene-level spatial reconstruction, allowing specialized models to fully exploit their respective strengths.
•
We introduce an
RPF-based geometric aligner
that formulates scene construction as an object-level point cloud registration problem and establishes geometric correspondence between object assets and partial scene point clouds, enabling explicit transformation estimation from the object-local coordinate system to the scene coordinate system.
•
We systematically validate the effectiveness and scalability of compositional scene construction. Controlled comparisons show that explicit geometric composition improves scene geometric quality even with identical object assets, while experiments with different object generation models demonstrate that the proposed workflow can independently benefit from advances in upstream 3D object generation.
2
Related Work
2.1
Single-object image-to-3D generation
Image-to-3D models provide object-local geometry, texture, and topology that can serve as reusable asset priors. Representative systems improve object-level shape quality, material synthesis, native mesh generation, or generation efficiency
(
Tencent Hunyuan3D Team, 2025
;
Xiang et al., 2025
;
Wang et al., 2026a
;
Xu et al., 2026
)
. Image-generation models such as FLUX-2, GPT-Image-2, and Gemini Image can further provide completed object images before asset generation
(
Black Forest Labs, 2025
;
OpenAI, 2026
;
Google, 2025
)
. These advances change the role of object generation in scene construction: rather than requiring a scene model to synthesize every asset internally, a compositional system can obtain an object-local mesh from a specialized provider and focus separately on scene placement. In our formulation, these models serve as upstream providers. Easy-3Dfy does not claim to improve their outputs; it discards every provider pose or layout output and estimates a local-to-pointmap-scene transformation from scene geometry.
2.2
Monocular geometry estimation and point-cloud alignment
Geometry reconstruction models such as DUSt3R, VGGT,
π
3
\pi^{3}
, Lotus-2, MogeV2 and Depth Anything V3 estimate depth, pointmaps, normals, camera parameters, or ray representations from input images
(
Wang et al., 2024
;
Wang et al., 2025a
;
Wang et al., 2026b
;
He et al., 2026
;
Wang et al., 2025b
;
Lin et al., 2025
)
. These outputs provide scene-level visible geometry, but do not directly define an object’s complete layout because of partial visibility, depth uncertainty, and object boundaries. Classical and learned registration methods recover rigid or similarity transforms from correspondences, local features, or iterative refinement
(
Fischler and Bolles, 1981
;
Besl and McKay, 1992
;
Qin et al., 2022
)
. However, when registering partial point clouds derived from monocular depth estimates to full point clouds produced by 3D generative models, their effectiveness can be limited by the domain gap between the two geometry sources. Generative registration methods such as RPF and RAP offer a complementary formulation for ambiguous and partial point-cloud alignment
(
Sun et al., 2025
;
Pan et al., 2025
)
. Easy-3Dfy uses an RPF-based direct layout aligner, but shifts its role from generic registration to object-level geometric composition: rendered partial observations and layout augmentation provide alignment supervision without requiring complete calibrated scenes for the alignment stage. Rather than seeking a new general-purpose registration backbone, we train a registration module specialized for single-image 3D scene construction, matching partial query point clouds extracted from monocular pointmaps to object-local anchor geometry.
2.3
Single-image 3D scene generation and layout prediction paradigms
Existing single-view scene-generation systems combine object assets and layouts in different ways. Joint methods generate multiple assets and relative poses in one end-to-end process, thereby exploiting global image context while coupling asset generation, layout prediction, and scene-level supervision. Two-stage or post-hoc systems instead assemble objects after asset generation using geometric, physical, differentiable render-and-compare, or relation-aware constraints. CAST, 3D-RE-GEN, MIDI, SceneGen, and SAM-3Dfy exemplify distinct points in this design space
(
Yao et al., 2025
;
Sautter et al., 2025
;
Huang et al., 2025
;
Meng et al., 2025
;
SAM 3D Team et al., 2025
)
. These systems commonly operate under an object-conditioned protocol with automatic, user-provided, or precomputed masks. Scene-Maker first decouples the de-occlusion model from 3D object generation; however, it still relies on scene-level supervision to enhance layout prediction performance
(
Shi et al., 2025
)
. Easy-3Dfy more strictly decouples object-asset generation from geometric alignment: it retains reusable asset and geometry priors, discards provider layout outputs, and learns the remaining local-to-pointmap-scene composition directly in the point-cloud domain.

4.3
Ablations
We ablate three components that determine the final constructed scene: the geometric preprocessing and input channels of RPF, the pointmap and occlusion-aware completion models, and the object mesh provider. These studies respectively measure sensitivity to the design of the alignment module , scene-geometry estimation and object completion, and asset quality.
Alignment design.
We further ablate point-cloud preprocessing and RPF input channels. Rule-based cleaning suppresses boundary and interpolation noise but may also remove useful geometry. As RPF is trained on augmented data and tolerates moderate noise, omitting cleaning has only a small effect at the reported precision, primarily a slight decrease in Scene-FScore. Removing surface-normal conditioning degrades all three layout metrics. Full results appear in Appendix
A.4
.
Scene geometry and object completion.
Beyond the mesh provider, we compare different pointmap and occlusion-aware completion models in Table
3
, using Meshy-T2 as the common mesh provider. All reported variants use the six-channel XYZ–normal RPF input. The controlled runs cover MogeV2 with FLUX-2 and GPT-Image-2 on both datasets, as well as DAv3 with FLUX-2. GPT-Image-2 slightly improves the scene-level metrics on 3D-FUTURE200 but does not consistently improve the object-level metrics or the results on Scene-Maker, indicating that the effect of the completion model is dataset- and metric-dependent. Refer to Appendix
A.4
for full results.
Mesh-provider comparison.
Figure

Full-scene views highlight improvements in scale, extent, and placement, while close-ups highlight texture and fine-detail quality. More advanced 3D mesh generators not only produce higher-quality textures, but also recover finer-grained surface geometry, such as the orientation of limbs for articulated objects including humans and animals. Moreover, these models often provide more accurate estimates of the object’s extent along the depth direction, resulting in object dimensions and aspect ratios that better match the geometric distribution observed in the pointmap. Such meshes provide more faithful surface cues for correspondence and can therefore yield more accurate transformation estimates during subsequent alignment. 5
Analysis and Metric Interpretation
5.1
What does direct alignment improve?
Figure
5
compares these methods with matched inputs and views, exposing differences in the scale, orientation, ordering and relationships of contact of the object. MIDI (trained on 3D-FRONT) and SceneGen (trained on 3D-FUTURE) generally recover the object categories in a multi-object image, but often distort relative orientation, ordering, and spacing in openset.
Compared with previous methods, SAM-3Dfy is able to predict the approximate positions and ordering of objects in the scene in an open-set setting. However, as shown in Figure
5
, its predicted layouts still exhibit noticeable geometric inconsistencies. Some objects suffer from interpenetration, such as the pillow floating behind the sofa backrest, while the tabletop and chairs are not properly aligned with the flat ground plane. These artifacts indicate that SAM-3Dfy still struggles to preserve fine-grained spatial relationships and contact relationships between objects. Using the same SAM-3Dfy meshes, Easy-3Dfy instead registers each asset to its pointmap-derived partial query, substantially improving the spatial consistency of object layout and resolving the aforementioned ambiguities of spatial relationships.
Note that small or severely occluded objects, contaminated masks, and unreliable pointmaps for reflective or transparent surfaces can leave the transform underconstrained, producing an inaccurate pose. Appendix
A.7
analysis failure patterns of these cases.
5.2
Geometric compatibility enhances attainable layout quality
Table
4
compares mesh providers under a fixed pointmap, mask, RPF model, and inference setting. Dataset GT meshes provide an upper-bound reference under the current workflow. The aligner works across all tested providers, demonstrating broad provider generality, while fine-grained layout remains sensitive to asset geometry. Dimensions and proportions that better match the partial observation improve geometric compatibility and facilitate alignment, whereas richer geometric detail or higher-quality texture alone does not guarantee a more accurate layout. This suggests that improvements in 3D asset generation can directly translate into more accurate scene alignment, without requiring any modification or retraining of the Easy-3Dfy aligner. 5.3
What geometry-centric layout metrics omit
The preceding ablations and analyses demonstrate both the effectiveness and the scope of the current evaluation. Scene-CD, Scene-FScore, and scene-aligned 3D bounding-box IoU improve with asset quality and registration accuracy, showing that they effectively measure geometric fidelity and spatial arrangement. However, they do not directly reflect appearance fidelity, texture and material quality, semantic identity, scene completeness, or perceptual plausibility. Even within geometry, point-set distances and bounding-box overlap have limited sensitivity to topology and fine surface structure.
The close-ups in Figure
4
and Figure
A1
make this boundary explicit: a scene can achieve a better layout score while retaining blurred textures or local details, whereas a visually detailed asset can remain geometrically incompatible with the observed scene. Future evaluation protocols should therefore combine geometric, visual, semantic, and completeness criteria to provide a more complete measure of generated-scene quality.
6
Conclusion
We presented Easy-3Dfy, a modular framework that formulates single-image 3D scene construction as object-level geometric composition across replaceable object assets, scene geometry, and metric layout alignment. To address the core layout-alignment problem, we train an RPF aligner on scalable object-level data to recover local-to-scene transforms, improving layout accuracy without requiring complete scene supervision. Experiments demonstrate consistent gains under the shared-mask protocol and applicability across mesh providers. We also identify limitations of geometry-centric metrics and motivate more complete evaluation protocols for generated 3D scenes.

Occlusion-aware completion prompt.
The completion model receives three reference images. We use the following prompt:

Structural completion and de-occlusion:

A.5
Additional visualization results
We provide additional visualization results in the Figure
A1
.
Figure A1:
Additional visualization results on 3D-FUTURE.
A.6
Inference Efficiency
The overall inference time of Easy-3Dfy is primarily determined by the runtime of its individual modules and the degree of parallelism. For example, completing a single object using the official FLUX-2-pro API takes on the order of tens of seconds. Low-poly mesh generators such as Meshy-T2 can produce geometries suitable for registration within 10 seconds, whereas more sophisticated models such as Hunyuan3D-V3.1 require approximately 1 minute to generate a complete textured asset. Our RPF-based aligner introduces only a small additional runtime overhead: it supports parallel inference and registration of multiple meshes, with each batch processed within a few seconds.
A.7
Representative failure cases
Layout estimation can easily become underconstrained or fail when object-specific partial geometry is severely degraded or insufficient. Such geometric information loss typically arises from visual challenges, including tiny object scales, severe occlusions, motion or defocus blur, and unreliable depth maps. As illustrated in Figure
A2
, different paradigms exhibit distinct failure patterns under these challenging scenarios: baseline methods (such as SAM-3D-like frameworks) often suffer from severe drift in scale and translation due to brittle pointmap regression, whereas Easy-3Dfy maintains much better spatial bounded bounds but occasionally experiences rotation instability when geometric constraints become severely underdetermined.

article.headline: 解耦物体生成与布局：Easy-3Dfy
article.lede: 把单图三维场景重建拆成物体资产生成与点云配准两步，用 RPF 对齐器估计布局，优于 SAM-3Dfy。
article.problem: 单图三维场景构建需要同时恢复完整的物体资产和它们在统一米制坐标系中的摆放。SAM-3Dfy 这类端到端方法把资产生成与布局预测耦合在同一场景级流程里训练，物体细节和空间布局的精细程度都会受限，常出现物体互相穿插、悬空、与地面接触关系错误等问题。
article.method: 作者提出 Easy-3Dfy，把场景构建改写为「物体级点云配准」问题：先用图像编辑模型补全被遮挡的物体区域，再交给可替换的图像到三维生成器产出物体局部网格；同时用单目几何模型预测场景点图与法向图，按掩码提取每个物体的部分查询点云。随后用基于 Rectified Point Flow 的 RPF 对齐器，以 XYZ 坐标加表面法向（六通道，不含 RGB）为条件，预测查询点在锚点云坐标系中的对应位置，再用 Umeyama 拟合恢复统一尺度的相似变换，把所有网格变换到场景坐标系完成组装。RPF 的训练数据来自物体级渲染：对齐的 RGB 与深度渲染给出像素匹配的真值对应点，并对查询侧与锚点侧分别施加随机旋转、缩放、平移以及遮挡增强。
article.results: 在 Scene-Maker（1000 个场景）与 3D-FUTURE200（200 个场景）上，Easy-3Dfy 与 SAM-3Dfy 使用完全相同的物体网格，因此 Object-CD 与 Object-FScore 一致（Scene-Maker 上分别为 0.188 与 0.695），差异只体现在布局：Scene-Maker 上 Scene-CD 从 SAM-3Dfy 的 0.261 降到 0.242，Scene-FScore 从 0.615 升到 0.649，BBox IoU 从 0.366 升到 0.399；3D-FUTURE200 上分别为 0.146→0.140、0.820→0.836、0.517→0.554。相比 MIDI（Scene-Maker 上 Scene-CD 0.442、BBox IoU 0.065）和 SceneGen（0.455、0.085），提升更明显。替换网格提供方时，以 Scene-Maker 为例，HY3D-2.0 的 BBox IoU 为 0.291，Tripo-V3 为 0.391，GT 网格作为上限为 0.415；去掉法向通道后 Scene-FScore 从 0.649 降到 0.641。
article.why_it_matters: 该工作把「能用更好的模型就换更好的模型」变成流程设计的显式目标：物体生成、场景几何、布局对齐三个接口都可替换，实测显示换用更强的三维生成器即可直接提升布局精度而无需重训对齐器。
article.limitations: 评测只覆盖 Chamfer 距离、F-score 和包围盒 IoU 等几何指标，作者自己也承认这些指标不反映纹理材质、语义身份、场景完整性和感知合理性。且掩码由数据集提供、不属本文范围；小物体、严重遮挡、反射或透明表面导致点图不可靠时变换会欠约束，出现旋转不稳定等失败；补全模型的影响还随数据集和指标波动，并不稳定为正。
article.figure_caption_zh: Easy-3Dfy 总览：给定物体掩码，空间模型预测场景点图，图像编辑器补全物体图像、可替换的图像到三维提供方生成局部网格，RPF 对齐器将其锚点云与点图中该物体的部分查询匹配，经 Umeyama 拟合恢复统一尺度相似变换，变换后组装成完整场景。

figure.caption: {Overview of Easy-3Dfy.} Given object masks, a spatial model predicts a scene pointmap. For each object, an image editor produces a completed object image and a replaceable image-to-3D provider generates a local mesh. The RPF-based aligner matches its anchor point cloud to the object-specific partial query extracted from the pointmap, predicts correspondence positions, and recovers a uniform-scale similarity transform via Umeyama fitting. Transforming all complete meshes assembles the final scene.

page_papers.title: FLOMSS: Generative Music Source Separation by Flow Matching
page_papers.abstract: Music source separation (MSS) has been conventionally addressed by discriminative methods. Recently, flow matching has emerged as a strong generative paradigm for modeling complex data distributions, with successful applications across diverse domains. These advances motivate us to systematically investigate flow matching for MSS in a four-source (Vocals, Bass, Drums, Other) setting in full-band stereo. Specifically, we investigate prediction targets, flow paths, single-source versus multi-source modeling, and mixture consistency constraints. Beyond the signal-level metrics commonly used for MSS, such as signal-to-distortion ratio, we further evaluate MSS methods using embedding-based metrics, as well as a listening test, providing a comprehensive benchmark. On MUSDB18-HQ, our proposed model exhibits competitive performance in both objective and subjective tests, highlighting the potential of flow matching for generative MSS. Demo: https://ik4sumii.github.io/FLOMSS/

Abstract
Music source separation (MSS) has been conventionally addressed by discriminative methods.
Recently, flow matching has emerged as a strong generative paradigm for modeling complex data distributions,
with successful applications across diverse domains.
These advances motivate us to systematically investigate flow matching for MSS
in a four-source (Vocals, Bass, Drums, Other) setting in full-band stereo.
Specifically, we investigate prediction targets, flow paths, single-source versus multi-source modeling, and mixture consistency constraints.
Beyond the signal-level metrics commonly used for MSS, such as signal-to-distortion ratio,
we further evaluate MSS methods using embedding-based metrics,
as well as a listening test, providing a comprehensive benchmark.
On MUSDB18-HQ, our proposed model exhibits competitive performance in both objective and subjective tests, highlighting the potential of flow matching for generative MSS.

37
]
.
Meanwhile, generative modeling has received increasing attention in related fields, such as in speech enhancement
[
26
]
, speech separation
[
30
]
, and music bandwidth extension
[
24
]
.
In MSS, recent generative methods primarily use learned source distributions for prior-based inference or conditional inpainting but generally do not explicitly learn mixture-to-source generative mapping.
For example, InstGlow
[
44
]
optimizes latent variables under independent source priors and a mixture likelihood;
Multi-source Diffusion (MSDM)
[
23
]
learns the joint source prior and performs separation via posterior sampling under the mixture constraint;
MGE-LDM
[
2
]
extends the multi-source setting, formulating source separation as a conditional inpainting in the latent space.
Although these works establish foundations for generative MSS, they do not produce full-band stereo audio, which is essential to high-fidelity music production.
More recently, flow matching (FM)
[
20
]
has emerged as a compelling alternative to diffusion for generative modeling. Unlike conventional diffusion-based training, flow matching learns continuous transports by regressing velocity fields along predefined probability paths. Optimal-transport or rectified paths can offer straighter trajectories, faster sampling, and strong generalization
[
35
]
.
These advantages have begun to transfer to audio separation: flow-matching models have been introduced for language-queried target sound separation
[
42
]
, speech enhancement
[
18
,
38
]
, and speech source separation
[
30
]
. More recently, SAM Audio
[
32
]
conditions a flow-matching model on text, visual, or temporal prompts for open-domain audio separation, including musical instrument extraction.
However, flow matching has not been systematically studied and evaluated for MSS, which targets predefined musical stems in full-band stereo mixtures
[
1
,
21
,
27
]
, unlike common speech-separation settings that separate multiple speakers from monaural mixtures
[
30
]
.
In this paper, we study supervised conditional flow matching (CFM) models for full-band stereo MSS, which separate a song into four sources:
Vocals
,
Bass
,
Drums
, and
Other
, where the
Other
source contains all remaining sources. We train and evaluate our models on MUSDB18-HQ
[
25
]
. We further extend the evaluation beyond signal-to-distortion ratio (SDR) by introducing spectral and embedding-based metrics based on pretrained semantic audio encoders and benchmark our models against prior discriminative and generative methods under these metrics.
Our main contributions are as follows:
(1) We introduce
FLOMSS
, an open-source
1
1
1
Will be open upon the acceptance
generative framework for full-band stereo MSS;
(2) We present a systematic study of flow matching for MSS, covering prediction targets, flow paths, single- and multi-source modeling, and mixture consistency strategies;
(3) We introduce a comprehensive evaluation for generative MSS covering signal-based and embedding-based metrics;
(4) We show that FLOMSS surpasses prior generative baselines and improves spectral and embedding-based metrics over a same-backbone discriminative baseline while achieving competitive performance compared with state-of-the-art discriminative methods.

4.1
Experimental Setup
Unless otherwise stated, all experiments are based on a 16M-parameter NCSN++ U-Net

We use the official MUSDB18-HQ

4.2
Evaluation Metrics
We use a collection of different metrics drawn from recent evaluations of audio generative models

Signal-based metrics.
We use spectral (STFT and Mel) and waveform L1 distance following DAC

All embedding-based metrics are computed using non-overlapping

Distributional metrics.
Different from LPAPS, which computes the pairwise distance, distribution matching metrics compare the sets of embeddings extracted from all 10-s ground-truth and separated segments. We report widely adopted Fréchet Distance (FD)

We conduct a listening test with WebMUSHRA

Conditions are anonymized and randomly ordered. For each method, we report the mean score across all participants and evaluated excerpts.
5
Results
5.1
Ablation Study with the Single-source Modeling
Table
1
compares the CFM formulations with the discriminative baseline and unprocessed mixture.
The discriminative baseline achieves the best waveform distance and SDR, whereas both OT-CFM variants reduce the Mel and STFT distances and improve most embedding-based metrics. Among the CFM variants, SB-CFM-
𝐱
\mathbf{x}
performs best on waveform distance and SDR but consistently underperforms the OT-CFM variants on embedding-based metrics.
Comparing the OT-CFM parameterizations,
𝐯
\mathbf{v}
-prediction achieves the best scores in embedding-based metrics, but yields worse SDR; whereas
𝐱
\mathbf{x}
-prediction performs better on all signal-based metrics.
We use OT-CFM-
𝐱
\mathbf{x}
for subsequent experiments because of its balanced performance across our collection of metrics.
5.2
Stepwise Behaviors
Fig.
1
compares the intermediate predictions of single-source model for Vocals using OT-CFM-
𝐱
\mathbf{x}
, with the discriminative baseline shown by dashed lines.
Early target estimates approach the discriminative baseline in Mel distance and SDR, suggesting that the model first recovers a reconstruction-oriented estimate that is closer to its discriminative version;
later estimates generally improve spectral and embedding-based metrics by sacrificing the SDR score, revealing a trade-off between spectral & embedding-based similarity and waveform reconstruction fidelity.
For the subsequent analyses, we retain all embedding backbones except OpenL3 and use FD as the representative distributional metric. Complete results for all evaluated metrics will be provided in our open-source repository.
5.3
Multi-Source Modeling
Table
2
compares single-source OT-CFM-
𝐱
\mathbf{x}
with its joint four-source variants.
The unconstrained multi-source model ( denoted as “w/o MC”) leaves the backbone size nearly unchanged and produces all four stems within a single model, rather than using four different single-source models. This efficiency in turn harms its separation quality, particularly on embedding-based metrics.
Adding the soft MC constraint described in Sec.
3.3
recovers most of the SDR loss, while preserving Mel and LPAPS.
Nevertheless, a hard MC constraint, either in the waveform domain or in the uncompressed STFT domain, exhibits an overall degradation, except with MERT embeddings.
Unlike
[
30
]
, we omit auxiliary signal-level losses to keep the training objectives consistent in our ablation study. This finding is limited to the waveform- and STFT-domain paths evaluated in this study and suggests that hard MC may require an MSS-specific flow path and training strategy. We leave this as our future work.
5.4
Benchmarking with Prior Methods
In Table
3
, we benchmark our FLOMSS (single-source OT-CFM-
𝐱
\mathbf{x}
) with existing generative and discriminative MSS methods. We note that these comparisons should be interpreted with care: SAM Audio and MGE-LDM were trained on different datasets, HTDemucs
[
27
]
was trained on MUSDB18-HQ augmented with 800 extra songs, InstGlow was trained on MUSDB18 augmented with guitar and piano stems from Slakh2100
[
22
]
, while SCNet
[
37
]
, Open-Unmix
[
34
]
and our models use MUSDB18-HQ training split.
In Table
3
, FLOMSS-S (16M) already outperforms prior generative baselines on most spectral and perceptual metrics under format-matched evaluation.
Compared with FLOMSS-S-Disc. (same-backbone discriminative baseline), it improves Mel and all embedding-based metrics, while yielding a slightly lower SDR score, consistent with the observed distributional–reconstruction trade-off in Table
1
.
Scaling to FLOMSS-M (67M) improves every metric and surpasses Open-Unmix on all metrics except SDR. Compared with SCNet and HTDemucs, FLOMSS-M achieves better Mel and FD scores on averages across all embeddings, while retaining a weaker SDR and slightly worse LPAPS.
We leave the further enhancement in SDR as the future work.
Last but not least, Table
4
presents the subjective quality of these MSS methods via a listening test described in Sec.
4.2
. Despite its lower SDR, FLOMSS-M ranked no.2 in the overall score, and ranked no.1 in Bass, no.2 in Vocals, and no.3 in Drums, indicating competitive perceptual quality.
6
Conclusion
We present FLOMSS, an open-source flow-matching framework for full-band stereo MSS, together with a systematic study of prediction targets, flow paths, single- and multi-source modeling, and mixture consistency. By extending evaluation beyond SDR to spectral and embedding-based metrics, we identify a distributional–reconstruction trade-off in generative MSS. On MUSDB18-HQ, FLOMSS surpasses prior generative methods and a same-backbone discriminative baseline on spectral and embedding-based metrics. It also improves Mel and FD over strong discriminative methods, although SDR remains lower. These results establish flow matching as a promising direction for generative MSS.

article.headline: 流匹配用于全频带立体声音乐分离
article.lede: Sony团队提出FLOMSS，用条件流匹配在MUSDB18-HQ上做四轨全频带立体声分离；感知指标提升，但SDR仍落后判
article.problem: 音乐源分离长期由判别式模型主导，近年生成式方法多依赖源先验或条件修补，很少显式学习“混合到源”的生成映射。已有生成式MSS工作也未覆盖全频带立体声四源分离，流匹配在该任务上缺乏系统研究。
article.method: 作者提出FLOMSS，在压缩复数STFT域建立以混合为条件的流匹配模型，系统比较OT-CFM与SB-CFM、速度/数据预测、单源与四源联合建模以及软/硬混合一致性。模型采用16M和67M参数的NCSN++ U-Net骨干，在MUSDB18-HQ上训练，推理用10步Midpoint ODE，并从SDR、频谱距离、FD/MMD和听测多角度评估。
article.results: 在MUSDB18-HQ上，FLOMSS-M平均SDR为4.34、Mel距离1.55、FD-VGG 0.65、FD-PaSST 205、FD-CLAP 0.24；FLOMSS-S平均SDR为3.77，高于InstGlow的2.75，但低于SCNet的9.69和HTDemucs的8.14。听测中FLOMSS-M平均分59.12、总排名第2，SCNet以62.59排第1；FLOMSS-M的Bass单项排名第1。
article.why_it_matters: 这表明流匹配生成式MSS不仅能超过先前生成基线，还能在同骨干下改善Mel与多种嵌入指标，为MSS评价从单一SDR转向感知与分布质量提供了证据。
article.limitations: SDR仍明显落后强判别模型（4.34对9.69），硬混合一致性约束在波形和STFT路径上整体退化，多源单模型也损害嵌入指标。与部分基线的训练数据不同，横向比较需谨慎；论文未给出推理时延等具体数字。

page_papers.title: Every Weight Is a Path of Shared Discrete Decisions
page_papers.abstract: We introduce TWIG (Tree-structured Weights with Inherited Gates), a representation in which every weight of a neural network is the end of a path of small discrete decisions: a sign, a shift by a power of two, a zero gate, an index into a shared table. Weights that belong together share the upper part of their paths, and each decision is inherited by every weight below it, so it is stored once and applied once. This simple change has three consequences. Any trained network can be written as a TWIG, and when the decisions are powers of two its weight layers become circuits made almost entirely of wires and adders, suited to chips whose weights are fixed at fabrication. Pruning, quantization, low-rank factorization, codebooks and weight sharing become edits of one object, so a single optimizer can choose among all of them for a whole network. And choosing the decisions is the ground-state problem of a higher-order Boltzmann machine whose interactions follow the paths of the tree, the problem class that annealers and quantum optimizers are built to solve. Today these questions are handled apart: each compression method brings its own format and solver, a circuit with fixed weights needs a dedicated constant multiplier for every weight, and discrete solvers reach only narrow subproblems such as rounding. Weight formats have long been moving toward shared decisions, through group scales, shared exponents, microexponents and sparse weights; TWIG takes this trend to its end, and every common format is a shallow TWIG at no extra cost. On five weight matrices of a large language model, a flat tree whose signed power-of-two terms are chosen per weight for circuit cost, with no group scales, needs 9--15\% fewer additions than GPTQ at equal layer error at 3- and 4-bit accuracy on typical matrices, and 20--55\% fewer on matrices with strong outliers.
page_papers.content:
Abstract
We introduce TWIG (Tree-structured Weights with Inherited Gates), a representation in which every weight of a neural network is the end of a path of small discrete decisions: a sign, a shift by a power of two, a zero gate, an index into a shared table. Weights that belong together share the upper part of their paths, and each decision is inherited by every weight below it, so it is stored once and applied once. This simple change has three consequences. Any trained network can be written as a TWIG, and when the decisions are powers of two its weight layers become circuits made almost entirely of wires and adders, suited to chips whose weights are fixed at fabrication. Pruning, quantization, low-rank factorization, codebooks and weight sharing become edits of one object, so a single optimizer can choose among all of them for a whole network. And choosing the decisions
is the ground-state problem of a higher-order Boltzmann machine whose interactions follow the paths of the tree, the problem class that annealers and quantum optimizers are built to solve. Today these questions are handled apart: each compression method brings its own format and solver, a circuit with fixed weights needs a dedicated constant
multiplier for every weight, and discrete solvers reach only narrow subproblems such as rounding.
Weight formats have long been moving toward shared decisions, through group scales, shared exponents, microexponents and sparse weights; TWIG takes this trend to its end, and every common format is a shallow TWIG at no extra cost. On five weight matrices of a large language model, a flat tree whose signed power-of-two terms are chosen per weight for circuit cost, with no group scales, needs 9–15% fewer additions than GPTQ at equal layer error at 3- and 4-bit accuracy on typical matrices, and 20–55% fewer on matrices with strong outliers. The properties of TWIG are proved; the measurements we report are first evidence on selected models and layers.
1

Introduction
Modern neural networks are trained in the continuum. Gradient descent needs a smooth landscape to follow, so weights are modelled as real numbers and learning is described as motion through a high-dimensional real space; much of what we understand about optimization and generalization rests on this view. Deployment, however, takes place in a discrete world. On digital hardware, every weight is a finite bit pattern drawn from a fixed format, every product is computed by a circuit of logic gates, and every byte has to be moved through a memory hierarchy. The passage from the continuous model that was learned to the discrete object that is executed is therefore unavoidable, and it has grown into a research field of its own.
That field has grown in pieces. Pruning removes weights, quantization restricts them to finite grids, low-rank factorization replaces matrices by products of thinner ones, codebook methods map blocks of weights to entries of a shared table, and weight sharing reuses parameters across layers. Each family brings its own storage format, its own solver and often its own kernel, and combining them (four bits in one layer, half of the weights pruned in another, a low-rank correction in a third) remains largely a matter of manual design, without a common yardstick. Two further questions sit almost entirely outside this picture. The first is the cost of
computing

Conclusion
Neural networks are trained in the continuum but run in a discrete world, and the passage between the two has so far been handled one method at a time. We have proposed to make this passage explicit with a single representation. In TWIG, every weight is the end of a path of small discrete decisions, and weights that belong together share the upper part of their paths, so that each shared decision is stored once and applied once. The idea is simple, and its consequences reach in several directions. The formats in use today are shallow state trees; nothing is lost in the worst case, and shared structure lowers the cost in bits. Read as a compressed model, a tree turns pruning, quantization, factorization, codebooks and sharing into edits of one object, chosen by one optimizer. Read as a circuit, it applies a layer with shifts and additions, apart from one scale per row and per column, with a size bounded by a count read off the tree. Read as an optimization problem, choosing its states is the ground-state problem of a higher-order Boltzmann machine whose interactions follow the paths of the tree, the problem class that annealers and quantum optimizers are built to solve. And because its decisions are explicit, a tree could be trained directly, so that the trained object is already the deployed one, a direction we leave open.

article.headline: TWIG：把神经网络权重写成离散决策树
article.lede: 一种树状权重表示把量化、剪枝、低秩与共享统一为对同一棵决策树的编辑，并试图把权重选择变成离散优化问题。
article.problem: 主流压缩方法各自带着存储格式、求解器和内核：剪枝、量化、低秩分解、码本与权重共享难以在同一框架下比较和组合。与此同时，用权重做计算的成本，以及离散优化器可触及的问题范围，长期被压缩研究分开处理。
article.method: 作者提出 TWIG：每个权重是一条小离散决策路径的终点，路径上依次有符号、2 的幂次移位、零门和共享表索引；同一组权重共享路径上部，每个决策只存一次、只应用一次。这样，常见压缩方法都成为对同一对象的编辑，可由一个在加性代价下精确的预算优化器统一选择；当决策取 2 的幂时，权重层可变成几乎只由连线和加法器构成的电路。选择这些决策则被表述为高阶玻尔兹曼机的基态问题，其相互作用沿树路径展开。
article.results: 在一个大语言模型的五个权重矩阵上，作者报告：扁平树（逐权重选择带符号的 2 的幂项、无 group scale）在 3/4 bit 精度、相同层误差下，典型矩阵比 GPTQ 少 9–15% 加法，强离群矩阵少 20–55%。在 LLaMA-3-8B 全模型上，3.25 bit/权重、无需训练的动态规划优化器将困惑度相对同管线最强 GPTQ 降低 14–17%，并在 WikiText-2 上把 GPTQ 与 FP16 的差距缩小 58%（从 1.95 到 0.81）。无损存储版本报告 12.133 bit/权重（磁盘）、运行时 12.137 bit/权重，转义权重占比 0.0095%（Llama-3.2-1B）和 0.0097%（Qwen3.5-9B）。
article.why_it_matters: 如果这些性质在实际系统中成立，TWIG 把压缩格式、电路实现和离散求解器接到同一表示上，部署权重不再只是训练后的压缩附属步骤，而可能成为可统一优化甚至直接训练的对象。
article.limitations: 作者明确说，报告的是选定模型和层上的首批证据，而不是普遍结论；部分结果将另文完整报告。论文的实测集中在模型压缩与无损图像编码，未报告固定权重芯片或退火/量子优化器的实测。

page_papers.title: HoloBoxing: A Simple Recipe for Humanoid Boxing with 7 Minutes of Single-GPU Training
page_papers.abstract: HoloBoxing presents a simple recipe for learning humanoid boxing by building on a pretrained whole-body controller. The recipe separates reusable motor skills from task decisions: a compact planner requests future body-point targets, while the frozen controller handles joint-level execution. A learned decoder maps 32-dimensional actions to structured target windows, and measured-state imitation initializes the planner before reinforcement learning. Task learning then refines interaction behavior while reusing the decoder and controller, avoiding the need to relearn whole-body control. This combination keeps task optimization focused on a compact upper policy and supplies an initial behavior before reward-driven exploration. Starting from that available controller, the recipe accounts for about seven minutes of additional training, including reused representation fitting and a single-GPU task run. This excludes controller pretraining, data preparation, evaluation, and search. Simulated boxing experiments and component controls evaluate the resulting behavior and the roles of imitation initialization and the target representation.

Introduction
A motion controller can reproduce a punch without deciding when or where to use it.
Humanoid boxing adds an opponent, changing contact, and the need to remain upright after an exchange.
Learning all of these behaviors from joint commands couples motor execution with task decisions.
HoloBoxing instead asks how far a simple, short training recipe can go when whole-body motor capability is already available.
Reusable whole-body controllers make task adaptation above existing motor capability a practical starting point.
The recipe separates what must be learned for boxing from what can be reused.
A pretrained HoloMotion v2 controller executes movement requests and remains frozen.
A learned target decoder represents short windows of future body-point poses with a 32-dimensional action.
A compact feedback planner selects these actions from measured robot state and opponent positions.
Task learning therefore adapts movement requests while retaining the underlying execution capability.
We initialize this planner through measured-state imitation before refining it with reinforcement learning.
The fixed controller first tracks reference motions to collect actual robot observations and future-target labels.
Supervised learning turns those pairs into an initial feedback policy.
Standing warmup and interaction against a fixed standing opponent then adjust behavior through rewards.
The decoder and lower controller are reused throughout, as illustrated in Figure
1
.
These choices make the training problem smaller in three concrete ways.
Controller reuse removes joint-level motor learning from task adaptation.
The target representation reduces the planner’s action dimension from 225 coordinates to 32 latent variables.
Imitation supplies an initial behavior before reward-driven exploration.
Together, they define the simple recipe whose training cost and resulting behavior we evaluate.
The primary recipe accounts for 7.0 minutes, combining a new single-RTX-4090 run with previously recorded target-representation fitting. A 21.4-minute long version provides a higher-budget comparison.
Simulation experiments assess whether this short adaptation produces interactive boxing, while matched-budget controls remove imitation initialization or the target decoder.
We also test observation choices and representation quality to explain the interfaces used by the recipe.
Detailed timings and competitive outcomes appear in the experiments; assumptions and remaining validation needs are discussed separately.

Background and motivation
Humanoid boxing combines motor execution with decisions about approaching, striking, and responding to an opponent.
Our focus is the additional learning needed when a general-purpose controller already supplies whole-body movement.
Three established ideas motivate a simple task-adaptation recipe.
Reuse motor capability.
Motion imitation learns physically simulated movement from reference trajectories
(
Peng et al., 2018
;
Luo et al., 2023
)
.
Recent humanoid systems extend this approach toward reusable whole-body control
(
Fu et al., 2024
;
Luo et al., 2025
;
Chen et al., 2026a
)
.
A task policy can request movement while a fixed controller converts those requests and robot feedback into joint commands.
HoloBoxing uses the released HoloMotion v2 controller in this role.
The boxing planner therefore learns task decisions above existing motor capability, rather than relearning joint-level execution.
This separation also defines the cost boundary: we measure new task training and exclude the inherited controller’s pretraining.
The task-specific problem is consequently to choose useful movement requests in response to an opponent.
This differs from acquiring a broad motor repertoire and motivates evaluating adaptation time separately from controller development.
Represent movement requests compactly.
Latent representations organize reusable movements and skills
(
Peng et al., 2022
;
Tessler et al., 2023
;
Zhu et al., 2023
)
, including spherical representations for state-conditioned motor control
(
Tan et al., 2026
)
.
HoloBoxing learns a decoder from a normalized 32-dimensional action to 225 future body-point target coordinates.
This gives the planner a compact action interface while retaining the same lower controller.
The representation supplies target structure, while the controller supplies motor feedback.
Since reconstruction quality alone does not establish physical executability, we evaluate both target error and tracking behavior.
The decoder and controller play different roles: one structures future requests, while the other responds to the robot’s current physical state.
Keeping these roles separate lets the task policy reuse both interfaces as learning progresses.
Initialize before learning interaction.
Imitation supplies an initial behavior, and reinforcement learning adjusts it through executed interaction.
Sports and boxing systems combine motion knowledge with task objectives in several forms
(
Ren et al., 2025
;
Chen et al., 2026b
;
Zhang et al., 2026
;
Wang et al., 2026
;
Luo et al., 2024
;
Yin et al., 2026
)
.
Adapting frozen motor models also provides a reusable basis for new behaviors
(
Vainshtein et al., 2026
;
Park et al., 2026
)
.
HoloBoxing initializes its planner from measured robot observations collected during reference tracking, then refines it through standing warmup and interaction rewards.
The decoder and whole-body controller remain frozen throughout task learning.
Measured observations matter because the executing robot can deviate from the reference trajectory.
Training the planner on these states connects its initial behavior to the feedback available during interaction.
Reinforcement learning can then focus on adapting that behavior to task rewards.
Together, these choices confine task adaptation to a compact feedback planner with an initial behavior and a reusable execution interface.
The experiments measure the training cost and boxing behavior of this combined recipe.
Component controls examine its ingredients without assuming a separate causal speedup from each one.

Refine task decisions while retaining motor execution
Proximal policy optimization (PPO)
(
Schulman et al., 2017
)
first runs 32 standing-warmup updates against a passive opponent.
The resulting weights and observation statistics initialize 128 interaction updates with fresh optimization state.
The primary recipe uses a fixed external standing actor as its opponent throughout. The same opponent and its original observation statistics are shared by both component removals.
Its reward combines task shaping and adversarial motion style
(
Peng et al., 2021
)
with weights 0.8 and 0.2.
Task terms guide approach, facing, contact, and balance; the match referee separately determines competitive outcomes.
The planner, value estimator, and style discriminator train during task learning.
The target decoder and HoloMotion controller stay frozen.
The value estimator predicts future reward, and the discriminator compares simulated motion with reference examples.
Reinforcement learning therefore refines task decisions while retaining the target representation and motor capability.

Evaluating short task adaptation
The evaluation asks whether the reused hierarchy produces interactive boxing after the recorded short training procedure.
It measures training time, competitive behavior, and the effects of removing task-policy components.
These measurements address different parts of the recipe: time quantifies adaptation cost, while behavior tests what that budget achieves.
All evaluated policies share the packaged robot, actuator settings, arena, simulator, and referee.
They retain different observation definitions, so the league is not an observation-controlled comparison of methods.
A valid hand contact scores a point, while a sustained fall can end the bout with a knockout.
We retain contacts and falls alongside match outcomes because an opponent can lose without receiving a scored punch.
Every bout lasts at most sixty seconds.
A fixed ten-round league gives each policy the same opponent coverage, with randomized sides and recorded initial-state seeds.
Elo summarizes outcomes within this frozen participant pool; component controls provide comparisons within the HoloBoxing recipe.
Recorded states, actions, and referee events allow replay without rerunning simulation.

specifies scoring thresholds, the rating equation, and replay conditions.

Discussion
Why the recipe is simple.
HoloBoxing assigns motor execution, target structure, and task decisions to separate components.
The pretrained controller supplies feedback-based movement execution, while the decoder turns compact actions into requests that controller can follow.
Measured-state imitation connects robot observations to those requests before task rewards refine the planner.
The same interfaces persist across stages, so task adaptation reuses the decoder and controller instead of rebuilding their capabilities.
Why short adaptation is possible.
The recipe confines task learning to the upper policy and its training objectives.
A 32-dimensional action replaces direct prediction of 225 future-target coordinates, and supervised examples provide the initial feedback behavior.
The recorded cost shows that representation fitting and initialization occupy a small part of the selected training path.
Most recorded training time is spent on standing and interaction, after reusable execution and target structure are already available.
This explains the allocation of work; it does not establish an isolated causal speedup for each design choice.
What the experiments show.
The seven-minute training path produces scored boxing interaction and ranks second in the evaluated pool. The 21.4-minute long version ranks first.
With 128 final-stage updates, the 7-min version yields stronger league outcomes than either component removal.
The representation studies also show why a low reconstruction loss alone is insufficient: the selected targets must remain physically executable.
Together, the experiments assess how the recipe’s interfaces and initialization support the behavior obtained within its budget.
Limitations and future work.
The study uses a small motion corpus and one selected task-training seed.
The reported time measures additional learning above an available general-purpose controller, excluding its pretraining, preparation, and search.
The primary learner also reuses a task-specific standing opponent whose original training is excluded.
This is a task-adaptation comparison; methods may inherit different motor capabilities and representations.
Independent seeds and matched timing studies are needed to isolate component effects on learning speed.
The direct-target control changes action dimension and exploration geometry along with removing the decoder.
The league is not a fully controlled comparison: methods retain different state encodings, history, and auxiliary inputs.
Our upper planner retains 78 observation features, but the frozen lower controller also consumes robot feedback.
A smaller upper-policy input therefore does not establish a smaller information budget for the complete system.
External policies also receive no destination fine-tuning.
League outcomes consequently describe these checkpoint systems rather than establish method superiority.
Our efficiency result is minute-scale additional training above reusable motor control; the available budgets do not establish a universally fastest method.
Terminal wins also require contact and fall statistics because a knockout can follow an opponent’s unforced fall.
Future work should broaden motion and reset coverage and test alternative lower controllers.
The current experiments are simulation-only; real-robot boxing and transfer remain untested.

Conclusion
HoloBoxing combines a pretrained whole-body controller, a compact target representation, measured-state imitation, and task reinforcement learning.
Its simplicity comes from separating motor execution from task decisions and reusing the controller and decoder throughout task adaptation.
The latent target interface reduces the planner’s action dimension, while imitation supplies an initial behavior before reward-driven interaction.
The primary recipe accounts for about seven minutes of additional training above an available controller. A 21.4-minute long version improves league outcomes at greater training cost.
Boxing experiments demonstrate scored interaction, and matched-budget controls examine the roles of initialization and target representation.
The study supports this combined recipe under the measured conditions; it does not isolate each component’s contribution to training speed.

article.headline: 冻结控制器上加7分钟，人形拳击出可用策略
article.lede: HoloBoxing在冻结的整体身体控制器上只训练上层规划器，计入复用的目标先验拟合后总训练成本为7.0分钟。
article.problem: 人形机器人拳击既要执行动作，又要做任务决策；如果直接针对关节指令学习全部行为，就会把运动执行与任务选择耦合在一起，需要重新学习全身控制。论文要问的是：当通用全身控制器已经可用时，一个简短的任务适配配方能走多远。
article.method: 方法冻结HoloMotion v2控制器，只学习一个把32维动作解码为225个未来身体点坐标（5个身体点×5个未来时刻）的目标解码器，以及一个输入1095维的紧凑反馈规划器；规划器实际保留63个当前自身特征和15个对手位置特征。先用控制器跟踪参考动作，采集实机观测与未来目标做实测状态模仿初始化，再用PPO经32次站立热身和128次交互更新精炼。
article.results: 计入复用的目标先验拟合47.2秒后，主配方总训练时间为422.2秒（7.0分钟），其中新流程本身375.0秒，模仿初始化6.7秒、站立热身84.9秒、交互学习275.3秒；21.4分钟长版本改用256次交互更新。在150场仿真对局的六策略联赛中，7分钟版本Elo 1541、26胜17负7平列第二，长版本1669列第一；对GGSD为7胜3负，对RoboStriker为4胜6负，且4场胜利中没有任何被判定的手部击打接触。同预算消融中，去掉潜在解码器Elo 1428、去掉模仿初始化Elo 1362。观察研究里，带对手输入的当前状态输入验证损失0.44447，比十帧历史加对手输入的0.53513低16.9%；选定表示与未压缩目标各完成81个验证窗口中的80个。
article.why_it_matters: 它把“任务适配”和“运动能力获取”的成本划清，说明在已有通用全身控制器的条件下，分钟级的单卡训练就足以产出有交互行为的拳击策略，为上层策略复用下层控制器提供了一个可复现的基线。
article.limitations: 训练成本不含控制器预训练、数据准备、评估与超参搜索，且复用了外部站立对手但未计入其训练；动作语料较小，任务训练只用单一种子。联赛并非受控比较：各方法保留不同观测编码与历史，移除解码器同时改变了动作维度与探索几何，长版本还在RTX 5090上运行；全部实验限于仿真，真机迁移未验证。

page_papers.title: CineMem: Attention-Aligned Fine-grained Memory Retrieval for Multi-Shot Long Video Generation
page_papers.abstract: Autoregressive video generation relies on memory retrieval to model long-range dependencies. This capability becomes particularly critical for multi-shot generation, where models must reconcile substantial visual changes across shot transitions with persistent semantic continuity. Existing methods tend to perform memory retrieval at the frame level and share the same historical context across all query tokens, overlooking the heterogeneous information needs and leading to redundant retrieval and inefficient use of historical memory. To bridge this gap, we introduce CineMem, an attention-aligned fine-grained memory retrieval framework that combines online memory organization with query-adaptive retrieval for autoregressive multi-shot video generation. Specifically, guided by intrinsic memory-access patterns revealed through attention analysis, we propose an online-clustered KV cache as a memory organization strategy over all historical tokens, enabling semantic-aware memory grouping and more precise retrieval. In addition, we introduce a query-level retrieval mechanism that provides broader access to historical information under a fixed retrieval budget, thereby improving long-term memory utilization. Together, these designs enable the multi-shot video generator to preserve long-range consistency across shot transitions, particularly in revisitation scenarios, while approximating full-memory access under a constrained memory budget. To facilitate evaluation, we further introduce a suite of task-specific, VLM-assisted metrics for faithful inter-shot consistency assessment. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework.

Abstract
Autoregressive video generation relies on memory retrieval to model long-range dependencies. This capability becomes particularly critical for multi-shot generation, where models must reconcile substantial visual changes across shot transitions with persistent semantic continuity.
Existing methods tend to perform memory retrieval at the frame level and share the same historical context across all query tokens, overlooking the heterogeneous information needs and leading to redundant retrieval and inefficient use of historical memory.
To bridge this gap, we introduce CineMem, an attention-aligned fine-grained memory retrieval framework that combines online memory organization with query-adaptive retrieval for autoregressive multi-shot video generation.
Specifically, guided by intrinsic memory-access patterns revealed through attention analysis, we propose an online-clustered KV cache as a memory organization strategy over all historical tokens, enabling semantic-aware memory grouping and more precise retrieval.
In addition, we introduce a query-level retrieval mechanism that provides broader access to historical information under a fixed retrieval budget, thereby improving long-term memory utilization. Together, these designs enable the multi-shot video generator to preserve long-range consistency across shot transitions, particularly in revisitation scenarios, while approximating full-memory access under a constrained memory budget.
To facilitate evaluation, we further introduce a suite of task-specific, VLM-assisted metrics for faithful inter-shot consistency assessment. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework.
